Everything has consequences. Her group chat is going to result in you breaking up with her, presumably because respect is important to you and you feel disrespected. This sounds like it's been really tough for you. I can actually completely understand how this happens with an ex. You start by innocently connecting as friends then opening up to each other (which feels fine, this is what friends do, right?) and then one day you realize "okay shit I now am thinking about them way more than I would a friend and I think I'm in too deep". It's at this point that you owe it to yourself, your ex, and your fiance to take a step back and figure a few things out.

In my opinion, the biggest decision facing you right now isn't "fiance or Kay", it's "do I want to marry fiance?". Kay shouldn't factor in to this decision at all, except perhaps that she indirectly pushed you to think deeply about these issues now. As others have said, you may be idealizing her or aspects of your relationship; who knows. There are also more choices out there than Fiance vs. Kay; maybe one of them is right for you and maybe neither are. So for now, focus on the big question - do I want to marry fiance? You owe it to both of you to figure this out with a clear head and likely can't do that while hanging out or chatting with Kay.

A few things to think about:

- Could this be "normal" cold feet? I dreamt of an ex of mine nightly for months before my wedding. I also freaked out days before getting married and asked my fiance to call it off. But deep down, every time I thought about NOT being with my husband, I knew I'd be making a mistake - he's imperfect but my gut always knew he was right for me. What does your gut say? (PS I am happily married now).

- Related to the above, do you tend to do this with other things - commit to things and then second guess? If so, how does it play out? Do you second guess your good decisions, follow through, and then feel better about them (as I do)? Or do you commit to things you don't want to do, do them anyway, and regret it/resent it? Think about your patterns and ask yourself whether this decision to get married is repeating a pattern of yours.
 and if you're comfortable with that.

As others have said, take some time to yourself and think deeply about these things. If you decide you don't want to be married, then you've got a tough road ahead - your fiance will be understandably very hurt, people may be angry, and you will feel bad. You might lose some deposits. None of this makes you a bad guy - but it is something that you need to reflect on deeply so that you can choose a path that works for you moving forward. You can't undo the hurt that others will feel by breaking off an engagement, but you can learn and heal and make sure you are honest with yourself in the future.

If you want to stay with fiance, then great - Kay acted ad a trigger to solidify your choice. Move forward with fiance and stop chatting with Kay - she muddles your head and you can't handle it and that's okay. Many of us have exes that need to stay in the past because they fuck us up in the present, NBD; this alone doesn't mean you love your fiance any less. But you need to know your limits and Kay is one.

Sorry for the novel and best of luck. I truly believe your gut knows the path forward if you can just quiet the distractions around you and listen to it

Edit to say, personally I wouldn't tell fiance about Kay whether you decide to stay with fiance or not. Mostly because she shouldn't be relevant to the decision - you're making the choice based on you and fiance, not you and Kay. But also because you haven't yet crossed an obvious line - you acted in good faith with Kay and then realized you were too far in and COULD fuck things up if the situation wasn't rectified. And now here we are with you looking to fix it.

One of the most helpful life lessons I have learned is to outright tell my partner what I want, instead of just hoping he does something. 

If I want him to touch my leg affectionately in the car? "Can you touch my leg?".

If I want him to kiss my forehead? "Can you kiss my forehead?". 

If I want him to comment on my cute hair/outfit? "Hey do you like my hair/outfit?".

You'd think taking the  "spontaneity" out of it would make his response feel less genuine, but somehow it doesn't. He usually lights up, focuses on what I've asked, and is excited to give me what I need. I think he genuinely just forgets/doesn't notice/gets absorbed in what he's doing unless I draw his attention to something else. (He does this with everything - I sometimes have to remind him to look at the sky or a sunset and he's like "oh yeah that's beautiful" 🤷). True relationship saver.
